title: Database Engineering & Internals
tagline: Storage engines, B-trees, LSM trees, query planners, and vector databases
description: Deep dive into database architecture: write-ahead logs (WAL), page buffers, B-tree vs LSM-tree indexing, query optimization, vector similarity search, and multi-model data storage.

stages.title: Stage 1: Storage Engines & Indexing Mechanics
stages.description: How databases persist data: pages, WAL, buffer pools, and index trees.

nodes.title: B-Trees vs LSM-Trees (Log-Structured Merge)
nodes.description: Contrasting read-optimized B-Trees (PostgreSQL, MySQL InnoDB) with write-optimized LSM-Trees (RocksDB, Cassandra, ScyllaDB).
nodes.whyItMatters: High-velocity telemetry and logging workloads can overwhelm B-Tree random-write I/O. LSM-trees convert random writes into sequential disk flushes.
keyTakeaways: B-Trees update pages in-place on disk, requiring Write-Ahead Logs (WAL) for crash recovery.
LSM-trees append all writes sequentially to an in-memory MemTable, periodically flushing to immutable SSTables on disk, which are compacted in the background.
LSM-trees provide superior write throughput but suffer from read amplification and compaction I/O spikes.
nodes.interviewTips: Explain write amplification and how Bloom Filters prevent unnecessary disk reads in LSM-tree databases.

stages.title: Stage 2: Vector Databases & HNSW Indexing
stages.description: Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) search, Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) graphs, and vector storage engines.

nodes.title: Vector Search Internals & HNSW Graph Indexing
nodes.description: How vector databases (pgvector, Milvus, Qdrant) index million-dimension vectors for sub-10ms nearest neighbor search using HNSW graphs.
nodes.whyItMatters: Exhaustive flat vector search is O(N) and stalls with millions of embeddings. HNSW provides logarithmic O(log N) approximate nearest neighbor lookups.
keyTakeaways: HNSW constructs multi-layer geometric graphs inspired by skip-lists: sparse top layers for coarse jumps, dense bottom layers for fine search.
Tune `m` (number of bi-directional links per node) and `ef_construction` to balance build speed vs recall accuracy.
Use pgvector when you already run PostgreSQL to eliminate the complexity of running a standalone vector database cluster.
nodes.interviewTips: Be prepared to compare IVFFlat (inverted file clustering) vs HNSW indexing tradeoffs regarding indexing speed, memory usage, and query recall.
